**Test image key features:**
- Whole tomato plant uprooted, laid on black surface
- **Very pale/white/bleached main stem** — most distinctive feature
- Entire plant severely wilted
- Brown/dying leaves
- Visible brown roots
- Some darker lesion spots on pale stem

**Reference image comparisons:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: References showed culture conditions with white mycelium and black sclerotia on stem pieces — while lab settings, the white/bleached stem coloration matches the key diagnostic feature
- **Southern_Blight**: Field views showing wilted plants at soil line — less stem bleaching
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Dark lesions on stem — doesn't match pale bleached stems
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Fruit spotting — doesn't match
- **Bacterial_Wilt**: Vascular streaming test — doesn't match
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Dark canker at soil line — stem above was green, not bleached

The **pale/bleached white stem extending along the main stem** is the defining feature. This is the classic presentation of **Sclerotinia sclerotiorum** (Timber Rot), which causes bleached, whitened stem lesions and results in whole-plant collapse.
